title: Age-weight the scope ratchet's ledger signals — the metric punished FILING, not rot
description: Closes the KNOWN METRIC FLAW filed with ED-IN-0112 and deliberately left unfixed there. `ed.open` and `ed.needs_jordan` were raw censuses, so they conflated WORK OPENED with WORK NOT CLOSED: appending a ledger row — the behaviour CLAUDE.md SS2 expects of substantively every PR — regressed the ceiling by one. A gate that fires on the correct action is a gate that gets ignored, and the baseline file predicted exactly that while shipping it anyway. I then compounded it by calling the flaw 'not load-bearing on M1', correcting myself that it IS load-bearing precisely during the queue drain, and still not fixing it. FIX: both signals are now AGE-WEIGHTED at STALE_DAYS=30. `ed.stale` counts open items older than 30 days; `ed.needs_jordan_stale` the same for the bottleneck subset. MEASURED on the 2026-07-31 tree: 213 open -> 76 stale (137 aged <=30d, 61 aged 31-60d, 11 aged >60d, 4 undated); 94 needs_jordan -> 21 stale. Targets re-derived rather than carried over (20 and 3, the latter following the measured ~1-in-6 genuine-taste share applied to the STALE subset rather than the whole queue). UNDATED COUNTS AS STALE (4 rows). An entry with no parseable date cannot be SHOWN to be fresh, and treating unknown age as zero is the same 'absence of evidence reads as a pass' defect this module already rejects for unmeasurable signals. SINGLE-OWNER EXTENSION, NOT A SECOND READER: obs_core.read_ledger_entries dropped `date` during normalisation, so age was unavailable to every consumer. Rather than parse dates separately in scope_ratchet — which would have recreated the exact second-ledger-reader defect ED-IN-0112's adversarial pass had just removed — obs_core now carries a normalised `date` (YYYY-MM-DD prefix, None when absent/unparseable so a consumer must decide explicitly). Every other consumer gains age for free. PINNED: a test that constructs BOTH cases and requires they differ — filing a fresh item must not move the stale count, a second rotted item must — plus one asserting an undated open row counts as stale. Neither can pass if the metric reverts to a raw census.

title: Standing gate: an adversarial steelmanned read-only review after EVERY milestone, not at the end
description: RULED (Jordan, 2026-08-04): 'use Fable 5 after every milestone/step to do an adversarial steelman read-only review for accuracy and logic and fidelity to plan'. Recorded in systems/_architecture/repository_keep_set_v1.md section 7.1 as a gate on every step of the evacuation sequence: a step is not complete until the review has run and its findings are applied or explicitly refused with a reason. WHAT THIS ADDS TO EXISTING DOCTRINE. CLAUDE.md section 10 already requires the agonist->antagonist relay and already wires valoria-critic (Read/Grep/Glob only, so independence is structural rather than declared, ED-IN-0087). It does NOT specify a CADENCE. This does: per MILESTONE, not per programme. JUSTIFIED FROM THIS PROGRAMME'S OWN RECORD, not from principle. Three defects in the separation work were found by adversarial passes and by nothing else, each invisible to the instrument that had just been built and pronounced sound: (1) the contest-groundup parity oracle sat in the evacuate set while a kept tool loads it to regenerate a committed golden a kept CI test asserts on (ED-IN-0130); (2) readers() could not see split paths, so the blocking-reader counts that sequence the entire deletion were blind to os.path.join construction -- 45 readers missed (ED-IN-0130); (3) deprecated/ holds 26 files of the BLOCKING ED-citation gate's universe, so the evacuation commit would have turned that gate red and the tempting fix would have destroyed the repo's only anti-fabrication check (ED-IN-0131). Each was cheap to check and expensive to have acted on. A single end-of-programme review would have caught all three AFTER the work they invalidate. THREE PROPERTIES THE GATE MUST KEEP or it decays into ceremony: (a) read-only BY CONSTRUCTION -- route through valoria-critic, never a prompt that merely declares read-only, since a sentence inside a prompt restricts nothing; (b) STEELMAN FIRST -- the reviewer states the strongest case for the work before attacking it, and 'this is correct and here is the best argument for it' is a valid verdict; (c) THE REVIEWER'S CLAIMS ARE CHECKED TOO -- reviews have been wrong in this programme (one reported id_reservations next_free unbumped when it was bumped; it had read a mid-session snapshot), so an audit is evidence, not a verdict. NOT YET ENFORCED. This is a convention with no guard. A CI check cannot observe whether a review ran, so the honest options are a per-step artifact under audit/ or a required line in the step's commit message. Filed rather than asserted -- per CLAUDE.md 0.1 point 5, if the guard cannot be written the pattern is not yet understood, and I am not claiming enforcement I have not built.

description: W4a of the separation work list (HANDOFF_IN). The clearest data-in-prose violation in the tree, named as 'the clearest inversion' by the fork plan §4.1 and unexecuted until now. WHAT WAS WRONG. systems/_architecture/key_type_registry_v30.md is a REGISTRY PARSED AT RUNTIME. keys.py said so in its own docstring: 'the registry markdown is the single source of truth... this class parses it at load time'. That was correct when the alternative was a hand-copied roster. It stopped being correct for two measured reasons. (a) GODOT RE-IMPLEMENTS THE LOGIC (Jordan, 2026-08-04) and cannot parse markdown; the port's answer today is godot/skeleton/data/key_types/*.tres -- FOUR HAND-MADE files covering 4 of 55 types, 93% incomplete before it starts drifting. (b) THE ROSTER HAS FOUR INDEPENDENT PARSERS, measured this session: engine/substrate/keys.py (TypeRegistry), tools/build_key_graph.py:136, tools/observability/build_graph.py:82 (parse_key_registry), and tools/dashboard_data.py:763 (a `### ` line counter) -- plus a hand-typed family table in dashboard_data.build_keys(). 'Every rule lives once' violated four ways on the most load-bearing registry in the repo, and every hand-maintained count had already drifted (keys.py's own docstring said 44 for a 55-type file, ED-IN-0134). WHAT LANDED. tools/export_key_types.py cooks the markdown to engine/engine_params/key_types.json, following the established typed-export convention (_generated header, schema_version, source, --check round-trip). It does NOT re-parse: it CALLS TypeRegistry.load, because that tolerant line-based parser IS the schema definition (the registry's ```yaml blocks are prose-flavoured -- unquoted colons and parentheticals make strict yaml.safe_load fail on real canonical entries), and a second parser here would re-commit the duplication the tool exists to end. TypeRegistry.load now DISPATCHES ON SUFFIX, so a caller switches source by changing a path constant and nothing else. ORD-1 PRESERVED, and this was nearly got wrong: keys.py:190 records that dict order IS registry order and significant. json.dumps(sort_keys=True) would have been byte-stabler and would have silently destroyed an ordering invariant. The export does not sort; byte-stability comes from the source order being deterministic. Pinned by asserting list(json.types) == list(md.types), not just dict equality. BEHAVIOUR PRESERVED, MEASURED NOT ASSERTED. The runtime reader (engine/cross_scale/echo_transport.py) now loads the JSON, and a seeded campaign returns hash c2da472354077b9c -- byte-identical to the value the fork build produced at the start of this session, before any of this work. FALSIFIERS (three, all green; 32 tests in the file). test_json_and_markdown_registries_are_identical -- the cooked and authored surfaces must parse to the same registry in the same order; this is the entire safety of keeping two surfaces. test_export_round_trips_byte_exact -- --check passes against the committed file. test_the_round_trip_check_can_fail -- POSITIVE CONTROL: plants a mutation in the committed JSON, asserts the checker exits 1 with DRIFT, restores, and then re-checks that the restore itself was clean so the test cannot poison the tree. Without it, --check passing would prove only that it ran. Also: the earlier roster pin was tightened from `>= 44` to exact three-way equality in ED-IN-0135 SPECIFICALLY so this inversion could not silently drop types -- that guard was put in place one commit before the work it guards, which is the point of the ED-IN-0132 cadence. The three TOOL-side parsers (build_key_graph, build_graph, dashboard_data) still read the markdown with their own parsers. Repointing four parsers in one commit is where mistakes happen, and the runtime was the priority. The inversion is therefore PARTIAL and this entry says so rather than claiming completion: markdown is still machine-read by three tools. W4b consolidates them onto TypeRegistry.load(JSON) and deletes dashboard_data's hand-typed family table. title: engine/params/ flips KEEP -> EVACUATE: the 43 parameter-table .md captured byte-lossless into YAML first; and the slice report's first sub-root evacuation exposed two false-positive scans
description: Jordan, 2026-08-04: 'params .md are largely useless at this point and I want them gone. code should have superseded them all by now' / 'just dump the constants to a yaml' / 'provenance can cite to a fork'. evacuation_plan.py's R-PARAMS-INFO rule said KEEP ('prose WITH a code pair -> information only'), justified by ~50 provenance referents from kept code that a deletion would orphan; the fork-citation ruling dissolves that objection, so the rule is now R-PARAMS-DUMPED (evacuate). WHAT WAS NOT ASSUMED. The census that motivated this -- 295 of 378 ALL-CAPS identifiers found in code (78%) -- is an OPTIMISTIC UPPER BOUND and its residue was noise (capitalised prose ALIGNMENT/DISTILLED, HTML markers AUD1, character names ALDRIC/MARET); a name appearing in code never proved its VALUE matched. So the deletion is NOT gated on that measurement. tools/export_params_constants.py captures the tables structurally (file -> section -> header + rows, cells verbatim, no invented schema -- typing them would be authorship) AND stores every file's full text in a `raw` map, making the capture lossless BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by my parser being total. It is not: six files (index stubs, history/) yield no table at all, which is exactly how a silent loss would have happened. Measured: 43/43 files captured, every one byte-identical to source, 258 tables, 1367 rows. THE GATE IS DELIBERATELY TEMPORARY. `--check` re-derives from engine/params/, so it cannot survive its own source; it is wired blocking in all four places (valoria-ci.yml, valoria_local.py, ci_checks_registry.yaml, test_gate_coverage.EXPECTED_COMMANDS -- the exact four-way omission that caused the ED-IN-0137 regression) and must be retired in the SAME commit that deletes engine/params/. No vacuous-pass-on-absent-source path exists, so forgetting turns CI loudly red rather than quietly green. TWO SCAN DEFECTS THE FLIP EXPOSED, both false-positive classes that would have made the deletion report unreadable. (1) engine/ is the FIRST root that only partly evacuates; readers() scanned kept files for the top-level directory, so a 43-file slice reported 'engine/' hits across nearly the whole tree. Fixed with slice_prefixes(): a slice is the shortest prefix under which NOTHING is retained. This also retroactively tightens tests/ and deprecated/, which had the same looseness. (2) joined_path_readers() counted a constructed path as a breakage if ANYTHING under it evacuated; tests/sim holds both evacuating stress prose and the KEPT canon mass-battle engine, so all 30 kept readers of the canon engine were reported as silent breakages. Now requires the target to be WHOLLY evacuating. Split-path alarms fell 33 -> 4, and the four remaining are real. RESULT (re-measured post-commit, when the 3 new files are tracked): 3153 tracked -> 1653 keep + 33 relocate = 1686 retained / 1467 evacuate. The pre-flip figure was 1693 keep + 33 relocate = 1726 retained, so the flip moves 43 files and the 3 new tool/test/data files return 3. CORRECTION (gate review F5): the first version of this entry wrote '1683 keep (was 1650)', comparing keep+relocate against keep-only -- an apples-to-oranges aside, and the kind of unreconciled number this ledger exists to stop. The headline share is unaffected: markdown share of the retained tree 51.9% -> 50.6%. The params tree was a small dent; audit/ (493 kept .md across 59 units, under Jordan's July rule) is 58% of all retained markdown and is the only remaining lever worth more than a percentage point. GATE REVIEW RESPONSE (ED-IN-0132 pass, verdict COMPLETE-WITH-RESIDUALS; fixes landed in the follow-up commit). F1 THE HEADLINE CLAIM WAS UNGUARDED: the exporter read text-mode with errors='ignore' and the falsifier verified with the IDENTICAL lossy read, so a CRLF line or an undecodable byte would be normalised/dropped on both sides and the pair would agree with each other while diverging from the file -- two lossy reads that match are not evidence of losslessness. Now reads bytes and decodes strictly (an invalid byte raises rather than vanishing) and the test compares raw bytes against the capture re-encoded. Measured: zero CR bytes across the 43 files, so the dump is byte-unchanged; what changed is what happens to a file that arrives before the deletion slice. F2 SCOPE GAP: the rule evacuates engine/params/** while the capture globbed **/*.md AND the test used the same filter -- guard and capture shared a blind spot (glob also skips dotfiles). Both now walk the tree; the exporter refuses to write if any file is outside the capture glob. Empty today, which is luck, not design. F3 THE CONTROL COVERED ONLY THE COMPLETENESS BRANCH -- it planted an omission, not a mismatch, so the byte comparison carrying the word 'byte-identical' had no falsifier at all, and this entry described the control as stronger than it was. Four content mutations added (cell delimiter, trailing newline, LF->CRLF, one digit). F4 a stale '1,996 files' survived in test_evacuation_plan.py's docstring in the same commit that changed the count to 1467 -- the ED-IN-0134/0138 stale-quotation class again, now removed rather than restated. F6 CLAUDE.md 5 still taught engine/params/ as the live number surface and listed the typed round-trip-checked export as 'not yet built'; amended. F7 the local references/evacuation_manifest.json was stale but is gitignored and untracked -- regenerated. F8 the reviewer swept for true positives lost to the scan tightening and found none. NOT ACCEPTED AS DEFECTS: nothing; all six actionable findings were taken.

title: Audit-family critique: which are load-bearing, and what the staleness metric actually measures
description: Filed as P8 during the W4 gate ("needs Jordan's call on which audit families are load-bearing"); this is the evidence for that call. Document: audit/2026-07-30-audit-family-critique/00_critique.md. HEADLINE. The vector audit IS the thing that identifies what is missing and nothing else in the repo computes it, AND its findings are near-stationary. Both are true at once and the staleness metric conflates them. MEASURED: over 8 days and 240 files of in-scope churn the feed moved 3 rows out of 178, in the improving direction (isolates 9->7, sparse_context 16->15; implied_missing 35 and notional 100 byte-stable). A freshness warning on a stationary backlog measures the wrong axis -- it says 're-run a script' when the message should be '178 structural gaps have gone unworked'. RECOMMENDATION 1 is therefore to INVERT what it reports (backlog counts, not drift), NOT to demote it; an earlier draft of this analysis recommended demotion and that was wrong, for the reason the two-axis split in the document's section 1 gives (content value and staleness informativeness are uncorrelated here). PER-FAMILY: mechanics-index is the one to promote -- it has NO generator, so its drift is editorial debt no script can clear, and it is the smallest number on the banner. vector-audit is highest on content value, lowest on staleness informativeness (both production paths regenerate the feed immediately before consuming it). graph-lexicon is low on both. decisions/proposals/apparatus are the governance observatory, NOT part of the vectorization review at all -- only vector-audit (its output), graph-lexicon (soft input) and mechanics-index (cited input) touch skills/valoria-vector-audit/. npc-audit should be reclassified: its artifact is an AUTHORED document, so 'stale' means a human must re-audit, sharing no remedy with 're-run a script'. THREE METRIC DEFECTS. D1: drift is computed from the artifact's last git COMMIT, not its last regeneration, so a no-op regen commits nothing and drift accumulates forever while the artifact is provably current -- not firing today (regeneration does change content) but silent when it does. D2: the weekly cron is nominally weekly, actually 1-in-3 -- exactly ONE scheduled refresh has ever landed (4029870, PR #244, 2026-07-27), the only commit matching the bot's own message; vector-audit and graph-lexicon last moved 07-22 and were not updated by the 07-27 run. D3: scope over-breadth manufactures the headline -- vector-audit's scope is most of the repo, so 240 files of churn produced 3 changed rows; the code carries a prior correction for exactly this failure mode at a smaller scope. THREE OF THIS ANALYSIS'S OWN HYPOTHESES WERE WRONG and were corrected by reading rather than grepping: ci_naming_check does NOT consume lexicon.json (it EXCLUDES it, skip-list at :70); review_core does NOT read apparatus_registry.yaml (comment only, :52); and the graph.json-pinned CI drift guard described at vector_audit.py:1215-1222 NO LONGER EXISTS -- the guard was rewritten to remove the dependency, so that docstring is STALE (recorded, not fixed: it is a skills/ file and this was a read-only critique). LIMITS STATED, NOT HIDDEN: notional (100) is untriaged, so the honest reading is 42 sharp findings (35 implied-missing + 7 isolates) + 136 needing triage, NOT 178 actionable; the stationarity claim is one regeneration at one commit; consumer analysis is static grep-then-read and would miss a dynamic import. Seven recommendations, ALL HELD -- none executed. PROVENANCE: the backlog counts and the 178->175 stationarity delta are reproduced by MEASURED-BY: skills/valoria-vector-audit/scripts/vector_audit.py (run with --emit-findings and diff against the committed feed); the per-family drift figures and scope definitions by MEASURED-BY: tools/audit_staleness.py; the regeneration-changes-content test for D1 by MEASURED-BY: tools/observability/build_decisions.py (run, then git diff --stat its artifact). Section 7 of the document carries the exact commands.

title: The keep/relocate/evacuate partition as a guarded instrument, not a prose table
description: WHY A TOOL. ED-IN-0127 authored the keep-set as prose. Prose cannot be executed or checked, and the specific failure being guarded against is one that PROSE CANNOT CATCH: build_fork.py's CARRY and LEAVE read like a partition and are not one. CARRY union LEAVE leaves a large NEITHER set (.github/, .githooks/, .claude/, tools/, tests/valoria/, most of references/, research/, skills/, CLAUDE.md, CURRENT.md, HANDOFF.md). Under EXTRACT the neither-set defaults to left-behind, which is harmless; under EVACUATE the mirror operation deletes it, taking the enforcement tier, the shipping gate and the session protocol. The defect was in NEITHER LIST -- it was in the assumption that two lists cover the tree. So tools/evacuation_plan.py refuses to emit a plan unless the partition is TOTAL over every tracked file. MEASURED: 3146 tracked files -> 1149 KEEP / 6 RELOCATE / 1991 EVACUATE. --check green: partition total; contract guard clean (no contracted or stub unit inside the evacuate set -- a unit with a contract but no code YET is the backlog, not dead weight). Per-slice blocking readers, which are what sequences a safe deletion: tests 73, audit 60, deprecated 24, proposals 16, workplans 16, arcs 9. A slice is ready when its blocking readers are zero or retired in the SAME commit. A THIRD VERDICT, RELOCATE (Jordan, 2026-08-04: 'visualization tool for mb should be moved to mb and wiring should be to systems folder'). keep/evacuate cannot express 'this is ours but filed in the wrong place'. Six MB instruments move to systems/mass_battle/workbench/ -- four from audit/2026-07-29-scenario-visualization/ (measure_colocation.py is the STANDING measurement behind ED-MB-0056/0059, not a session record) and two from research/diagrams/mass_battle_formations/. Precedent: systems/combat/combat_engine_v1/workbench/. Their rendered output does NOT travel; it regenerates from the relocated source. A DEFECT IN MY OWN FIRST DRAFT, found by probing rather than by review, and recorded because the shape recurs: R-AUDIT-GENSRC kept ANY .py under audit/ on the rationale 'a generator, not a record'. It was justified by FOUR visualisation generators and fired on 82 files, ~78 being stale April/May one-off session sims (mc_v10.py, pp686_sim.py, stage10_articulation_sim.py). A keep-rule 20x broader than its justification is precisely how a 'streamlined' repo quietly keeps its detritus. Deleted; ordering does the work instead -- generated output evacuates at any date, then the ordinary two-week rule applies to source, so in-window generators are kept because their session is current and stale sims leave with theirs. R-AUDIT-STALE 1040 -> 1087. DASHBOARD KEPT (Jordan, 2026-08-04), reversing ED-IN-0127's evacuate row. CAVEAT NOT YET RULED: the dashboard's INPUTS shrink -- it surfaces proposals/ BY LOCATION and reads workplans/, and workplans/ is still in the evacuate set with 16 blocking readers including tools/workplan_status.py (the SessionStart banner) and tools/dashboard_data.py. Keeping the dashboard while evacuating its data sources leaves a live surface reading missing files. Flagged, not silently resolved. FALSIFIER (CLAUDE.md 0.1 point 3): tests/valoria/test_evacuation_plan.py, 24 tests, MUTATION-VERIFIED 5/5. (M1) unmatched files default to keep instead of UNPARTITIONED -> 1 failed, caught by test_the_totality_guard_can_fail, the positive control that stops totality being vacuously true. (M2) undated audit entries treated as recent -> 2 failed. (M3) contract guard always clean -> 1 failed. (M4) relocation destinations point back into audit/ -> 1 failed. (M5) generated renders no longer beat the two-week keep -> 2 failed. Tool restored byte-exact after the run (cmp clean); control 24 passed. test_ordering_is_load_bearing pins FIRST-MATCH-WINS specifically: tests/sim/mass_battle/ matches both R-MB-CANON (keep) and R-TESTS-PROSE (evacuate), so a reordering would evacuate the canon engine while totality still passed. SCOPE: NO DELETION IS AUTHORISED BY THIS ENTRY. The tool computes and reports; it never removes a file, and says so in its own docstring. needs_jordan is TRUE for the per-directory line (the workplans/dashboard coupling above, skills/ triage, and the proposals/ per-file list).

title: Post-evacuation cleanup: 24 test failures -> 0, by deleting what lost its subject rather than repairing it
description: Jordan: 'Keep it simple, ie don't build tools unnecessarily.' A read-only review triaged the 24 failures left by the evacuation and found ONE genuinely broken kept tool; everything else was a guard outliving the thing it guarded. Disposition was DELETE by default. DELETED, subject gone: tests/valoria/test_params_dump.py (7 failures -- it existed to make the engine/params deletion safe, and that deletion is now merged; a safety guard for a consumed one-way door guards nothing). tools/ci_formula_prose_check.py + its test + 4 wiring points -- BOTH its inputs left main (the census and its entire live-scan surface), so it was a report-only gate printing 'no drift' over nothing, which its own comment records having happened for 14 days once already. 46 dead LANE_PATH_PREFIXES rows in build_decisions -- a lane-map row matching nothing does not fail loudly, it silently leaves the lane unassigned. Two one-liners: build_proposals' ranked_view (linked at an evacuated doc -- a link nobody can follow is worse than no link) and engine/params/ from validate_ed_citations' scan prefixes. FIXED, genuinely broken: tools/build_identifier_census.py imported parse_file from the retired export_params_constants and ImportError'd on invocation. The 'one owner' deferral was correct when written; deferring to an owner whose subject then leaves makes the dependency the defect. Parser inlined, ~20 lines, no second consumer to drift against. TERMINAL-STATE TEST CASUALTIES, the interesting class: four tests asserted against a NON-EMPTY evacuate set, which is now empty -- the state the tool was built to reach. Asserting the scan finds something is asserting the job is unfinished. Rewritten to plant their own inputs, so the property (a mixed prefix is not evacuating; a constructed path into an evacuating tree is found) survives the success of the thing it was watching. Same shape for test_wf_harness_check, whose fixture COPIED a wf_*.js retired with the evacuation: all 20 tests errored at setup. Synthesising a donor from the owner block was tried and rejected on measurement -- the gate enforces per-script rules a minimal synthetic script fails -- so the last real donor was restored from the fork ref as a committed FIXTURE. Data, not tooling. CLAUDE.md section 3 corrected: it still described arcs/ as a live primary, audit/ as organised into lane buckets that no longer exist, and engine/params/ as 'deletion lands in W7'. The deprecated/ row now records what SURVIVES and why -- the editorial-ledger archives are the BLOCKING citation gate's ED universe, and removing them would destroy the anti-fabrication check.
